what: A row of three hand-drawn black-and-white cross-section diagrams at the foot of the page (below the Activity block): (i) a hatched valley cross-section with a narrow V-shaped notch cut into it and a wavy water surface at the top of the notch, (ii) a hatched cross-section with a very deep, narrow, near-vertical slot cut through it, (iii) a plan view in which a channel arrives from the left (arrow showing flow) and splits into two stippled, fan/triangular sediment bodies with distributary arrows leaving to the right. The student must name the landform in each.

A full-page colour panorama (printed sideways) of a landscape running from a snow-capped, glaciated mountain range with a smoking volcano at the top, down through valley glaciers and a meandering river across a green plain, to a coastline with a delta, lagoons and beaches. The student must identify and number the landforms formed by the different agents of erosion shown in it.
